children: Accounting firm Deloitte has been fined £6.05 million ($7.98 million) over its audits of transport operator Go-Ahead Group for the financial years between 2016 and 2020, Britain's Financial Reporting Council said on Thursday.
The FRC said the financial penalty had been reduced from £11 million due to Deloitte's "exceptional cooperation" and admissions. Deloitte did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Deloitte's fine relates to overpayments made by Britain's Department for Transport to one of Go-Ahead Group's subsidiaries, London & South Eastern Railway, under a rail franchise agreement before Deloitte became auditor.
LSER retained the money and did not tell the Department of Transport, which eventually became aware in 2021 and took action to recover the overpayments.
The FRC said Deloitte had "failed to challenge the wrongful retention by (Go-Ahead Group) of over £30 million of public money for an extended period".

Penrose Foss, the FRC's Executive Director of investigations and Enforcement, said in a statement: "These breaches show a highly concerning pattern of failure by Deloitte to apply sufficient scrutiny to decisions and actions by (Go-Ahead Group) which were clearly questionable."
